question.text: Within how many days must a stock exchange grant or reject the in-principle listing approval?

explanation.text: The Logic: Stock exchanges must grant or reject the in-principle listing approval within 30 days from the later of the date of receipt of the application or the date of receipt of a satisfactory reply. For IPOs, in-principle approval must be obtained from all recognised stock exchanges where listing is proposed. The Trap: 15 days might be confused with other regulatory timelines such as refund or disclosure windows; the 30-day rule specifically governs in-principle listing approval. Note: The 30-day clock runs from the later of application receipt or satisfactory reply, not strictly from the date of filing.
